of practice partners to take part in shared care.
I have been left facing a five year wait for medication after being told by the practice that they would not be providing  me with my medication as I "chose to be seen privately" (practice managers exact words) to see a consultant when faced with a five year wait on my NHS referral. I now have the option of waiting for five years or pay a private Gp £30 a month the write the prescription for me, then pay a further £70 a month for the medication. I am not in a position to be able to afford that at this time and will have to go without and wait on my NHS appointment in order to be prescribed the same medication, then, the practice will give it to me as it was prescribed by an NHS consultant.
It is a choice for the practice not to take part in shared care, it isn't something that they can't do, its that they don't want to do it.
I spoke with one of the partners in the practice, Dr Dickson and told him of my concern, that I was facing a five year wait on medication. I asking why my care could not be shared between them and a private consultant, he said that the practice choses not to take part in shared care and that "it is more trouble than it is worth" It was Dr Dickson who initially referred me to the NHS and advised me of the wait time that I faced. He said I had the option to be seen privately, but failed to tell me that if I did, the practice would not supply the prescription.
I asked some questions in order to get a better understanding of why this was happening and to better get a true understanding of where the NHS is. He told me that its likely Gp practices will go the way of dentists and be private in around ten years or so. He also told me how long it has been since practice partners got a pay increase.
I am shocked and saddened by the health care system and can't believe how little some our Gp's actually care for us.
